parakeet: What if I told you that Christianity didn't just rewrite history, it rewrote logic itself. Before the church ever quoted Scripture, the word logos was the crown jewel of philosophy. It was the rhythm of the cosmos, the architecture of reason, the spark that lets humans rise above instinct and step into understanding. It was universal, democratic, accessible to anyone willing to think. But then came the Gospel of John. One sentence. And everything changed. In that single move, what at once belonged to everyone was privatized. Reason was no longer a public tool. It was a theological title. Truth was no longer discovered. It was handed down. That shift wasn't just clever theology. It was an ideological coup. By seizing the word logos, Christianity didn't simply join the conversation of philosophers. It ended it. It pulled reason out of the public square and locked it inside revelation. And the consequences of that move would shape the course of Western civilization for over a thousand years. This is the story of how Christianity usurped logic and why reclaiming logos today might be one of the most radical acts of liberation we can imagine. Before Christianity ever touched it, the word logos had a rich and layered history. It wasn't about scripture, it wasn't about prophecy, it was about something more fundamental: reason itself, the principle that made the world intelligible.
